s1.heading: I find out what is wrong. Then I build the fix.
s1.body: Every AI has different problems. I do not use a one-size-fits-all checklist. I look at your AI, talk to the people it affects, and build a solution that fits.
step1.heading: I talk to the people your AI affects.
step1.body: Before I look at the technology, I talk to the real people using it. They show me exactly where things go wrong.
step2.heading: I name the exact problem.
step2.body: Is the AI unfair to some people? Is it too confusing? I figure out exactly what is broken so we fix the right thing.
step3.heading: I build a tool your team can use.
step3.body: Not a long report. A simple, practical guide your team can follow. Something you can start using right away.
compare.heading: This is not a tick-box exercise.
compare.body: A compliance checklist tells you if you pass a test. It does not tell you if real people can actually use your AI. I find out what real people struggle with.
sample.heading: What does a framework look like?
sample.body: It is a set of simple questions your team asks before every AI decision. Here is a real example.
sample.a1: List every group. Include the ones easiest to forget: elderly, children, disabled, low-income.
sample.q2: Can they understand what the AI decided?
sample.a2: If a 70-year-old cannot explain the decision back to you, it is not clear enough.
sample.a3: There must always be a way to opt out or talk to a human instead.
sample.q4: What happens when the AI is wrong?
sample.a4: Every AI makes mistakes. Your team needs a plan for when that happens.
sample.a5: A framework only works if someone is responsible for keeping it up to date.
sample.note: This is a simplified example. The real framework I build for your team is tailored to your AI, your users, and your regulations.
example.heading: Example: TrustBridge
example.body: Banks, hospitals, and schools were building AI that left out older adults, children, and patients. I tested it with those real people and built a design system to fix it.
audit.heading: Example: The AI Trust Audit
audit.body: I run a short session with your team. We fill in a questionnaire and then talk it through together. I find out how your team really feels about AI -- what scares them, what they need, and what would make them feel safe. You get a clear report, a list of what to fix first, and paperwork that helps with EU AI Act rules.
cta.heading: Tell me what is going wrong.
cta.body: Write me a few sentences about your AI problem. I will reply within 48 hours.
cta.note: No commitment. Just a clear answer.
